html:
The Pinjarup, or Bindjareb, are an Aboriginal people of the southwest of Western Australia, around the Peel Inlet and the Murray River south of Perth. They are one of the language groups of the Noongar.

Their neighbours were the Whadjuk to the north, the Wadandi to the south and the Wiilman inland. The Peel estuary was rich in fish, and people built fish traps in its shallows.

After the Swan River Colony was founded in 1829, settlers moved onto Pinjarup land and clashes followed. In October 1834 Governor James Stirling led soldiers and police in an attack on a Pinjarup camp on the Murray River, killing many people. It is known as the Pinjarra massacre. The number killed is disputed, from about 15 to many more. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
